post.description:
Doc 07 §4.1 ``POST /auth/login``; response shape from doc 08 line 913.

200 rather than 201. Doc 08 shows ``200 { data: { accessToken, user, orgs } }``, and a
login creates no addressable resource, so there is no ``Location`` for a 201 to point
at. The Redis session is an implementation detail of the credential, not a REST
resource.

Doc 07 §7.3's rotation; doc 08 lines 964-966 (empty body, cookie travels itself).

A missing cookie is a 401, not a 422. Pydantic would call an absent required cookie a
validation error, but "you presented no credential" is an authentication failure — the
same one ``get_current_user`` raises for a missing bearer token — and routing it
through the validation handler would also produce a *different* envelope shape for the
same logical condition.

Doc 08 line 982: "revokes the Redis refresh session and clears the cookie".

Always 200, and the cookie is always cleared — even when no live session was found.
The caller's intent is "end my session", and that is satisfied either way; a 401 here
would leave the browser holding a cookie the server has already forgotten.

ADDED, and **unauthenticated by necessity**.

The invitee has no account, so there is no credential to require — the
invitation token *is* the credential, and it is verified by hashing it and
matching the stored digest. See
:func:`app.modules.tenancy.service.accept_invitation` for how the token's org
prefix is used only to satisfy RLS and is not an authorization input.

200 rather than 201. Acceptance may create a user row, or may join an existing
user to the org; the caller cannot be told which without learning whether the
invited address is registered, and a status code that varies by that is exactly
such a disclosure.

Returns no token pair. Reported as a judgment call: acceptance proves control of
a link, not of a password, and issuing a session here would make a forwarded
invitation email a bearer credential for the account it just created.

get.description:
Doc 07 §4.2 ``GET /orgs`` — "list user's organizations".

Not paginated, deliberately. Pagination exists to bound an unbounded result set,
and this one is bounded by how many organizations one person belongs to. Adding
``?page=`` would also mean the org-picker (doc 08 §6.5) could render an
incomplete list of the caller's own orgs, which is a worse failure than a large
response.

The identity this answers for comes from the verified JWT ``sub`` claim and is
never a parameter — see
:meth:`app.modules.tenancy.repository.IdentityRepository._self_memberships`.

post.description:
Doc 07 §4.2 ``POST /orgs``. Guarded by authentication alone.

There is no role that could be required here: in the bootstrap case the caller
has no membership anywhere, so ``get_org_context`` would have nothing to resolve.
REPORTED — this means any authenticated user can create organizations without
limit. A per-user cap belongs with the login rate-limiting work the brief
reserves for a separate task, so it is recommended in the report rather than
added here.

201 with the created resource, per doc 07 §4.2's REST conventions. No
``Location`` header: doc 07 §22 does not use them and doc 08's client reads the
id out of ``data``.

get.description:
Doc 07 §4.2 ``GET /auth/me`` — listed under the Tenancy module's routes.

Authentication only, and deliberately **not** ``get_org_context``. A user who
belongs to more than one organization logs in without an ``activeOrgId`` (see
``app/modules/auth/schemas.py``'s ``LoginIn.org_id``), so requiring an org
context here would 403 exactly the callers who most need to ask "who am I and
what orgs do I have?" before they can choose one. Doc 08 §6.5's org picker is
that flow.

``activeOrgId`` and ``activeRole`` are read straight off the resolved
``AuthenticatedUser`` — that is, off the verified JWT claims — and are ``None``
for an org-less token. They are reported as what the *token* says, not
re-derived from ``memberships``; the ``memberships`` list beside them is the
authoritative set, and a disagreement between the two is a real thing a client
should be able to see (it means the caller's role changed since the token was
minted, and ``POST /switch-org`` is the fix).

No re-decode here: ``AuthenticatedUser`` already carries everything this route
needs, so it does not pay :func:`access_claims`' redundant cost.

post.description:
Doc 08 lines 934-938 ``POST /auth/switch-org`` — re-mint with a new ``activeOrgId``.

Doc 08, verbatim: "User selects org → ``POST /auth/switch-org`` → API validates
membership → new access token with new ``activeOrgId``". The middle clause is the
whole endpoint. :func:`app.modules.tenancy.service.switch_active_org` performs it
against a real ``memberships`` row *before* minting anything, and derives the new
token's ``role`` from that same row — so this cannot be used to carry a role from
one org into another.

Authentication only, and again **not** ``get_org_context``: the primary caller is
a multi-org user holding an org-less token, and requiring an org here would make
the endpoint unreachable from the state it exists to resolve.

No ``Set-Cookie``. The refresh cookie is unchanged and stays valid — its stored
session is rewritten in place by ``tokens.retarget_family`` so a later refresh
does not silently revert the switch. See that function for why rewriting beats
revoke-and-reissue.

get.description:
ADDED (doc 07 §4.2 has ``GET /orgs`` but no single-org read).

Open to any member: doc 07 §8.1 has no row restricting an org's own members from
seeing the org they belong to, and a ``teacher`` needs the org's name to render a
header.

delete.description:
ADDED — soft delete. ``super_admin`` only.

Doc 07 §4.2 documents no DELETE route for anything. The most restrictive
available role is required because this is the most destructive operation in the
module, and because ``super_admin`` is doc 07 §8.1's platform role — deleting a
tenant is a platform action, not a tenant one.

See :func:`app.modules.tenancy.service.delete_organization` for what does *not*
cascade and the live consequence of that, which is reported rather than
half-fixed.

post.description: Doc 07 §4.2 ``POST /orgs/:id/branches``.

get.description:
Doc 07 §4.2 ``GET /orgs/:id/branches``. Open to any member.

A ``teacher`` scoped to one branch still sees the whole list here. That is
deliberate and worth being explicit about: doc 07 §8.2's ``branch_id`` narrows
which *data* a member may act on, not whether they may know the organization has
other branches — and a branch name is not tenant-sensitive within its own tenant.
Narrowing this list to the caller's own branch is a product decision, not a
security one, and doc 07 §8.1 does not ask for it. Reported.

patch.description:
ADDED (doc 07 §4.2 has no branch update).

No ``org_id`` in the path, so there is no path-vs-token check to make — and none
is needed. The branch is looked up through ``BranchRepository`` scoped to
``ctx.org_id``, so a branch id from another tenant simply is not found (404,
which doc 08's status table explicitly wants for "resource absent, **or scoped
away by tenant isolation**"). RLS is the second layer behind that.

post.description:
Doc 07 §4.2 ``POST /orgs/:id/invitations``, emits ``invitation.sent``.

The response carries the plaintext token because P1 has no mail sender. See
:class:`app.modules.tenancy.schemas.InvitationCreatedOut` for why that is stated
as a gap rather than presented as a feature.

get.description:
ADDED — the brief's "create/list/revoke"; §4.2 lists only create.

Admin-only, unlike the branch list. An invitation row carries an email address
that has not yet joined the organization, which is personal data about a
non-member; ``teacher`` has no reason to enumerate it.

The parameter is named ``invitation_status`` in Python and ``status`` on the
wire. ``status`` alone would shadow the ``fastapi.status`` module imported for
the ``status_code=`` arguments above — a name collision that would surface as a
confusing ``AttributeError`` inside an unrelated route.

post.description:
ADDED — ``POST ... /revoke``, not ``DELETE /invitations/{id}``.

Revision 0024 grants ``app_user`` ``SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE`` and never grants
``DELETE``, and ADR-004 forbids hard deletes in application code regardless. So
revocation is a status transition and the route names it. See
:func:`app.modules.tenancy.service.revoke_invitation`.

Registered **after** ``POST /invitations/accept`` is registered on
``public_router``, but the two cannot collide in either order: ``/invitations/
accept`` is two path segments and ``/invitations/{id}/revoke`` is three. Noted
because a future ``POST /invitations/{id}`` *would* collide with ``accept``, and
the resolution then is registration order — public first.

get.description:
ADDED — doc 07 §4.2 has ``PATCH /memberships/:id`` and no way to find one.

Admin-only per §8.1's "Manage users" row. This is the route that supplies both
the membership id and the ``rowVersion`` that ``PATCH`` requires.

patch.description:
Doc 07 §4.2 ``PATCH /memberships/:id``, emits ``membership.role_changed``.

``require_roles`` is necessary but not sufficient here — three further checks
live in the service (no self-modification, only a ``super_admin`` may touch
``super_admin``, and ``branch_id`` must name a live branch in this org). See
:func:`app.modules.tenancy.service.update_membership`; none of the three is in
any document and all three are in the report.

get.description:
Download a filled-example CSV template for bulk question import.

The template uses the canonical column names expected by the import
endpoint.  Fill it in and upload via POST /questions/import.

post.description:
Parse an import file and return headers + first 5 rows + recommended column mapping.

Use the returned ``recommended_mapping`` as a starting point.  Correct any
mis-mapped columns, then POST to /questions/import with the adjusted mapping.

Queue a question import from a CSV, XLSX, or JSON file.

A durable worker job is returned immediately. Each row is independently
validated and processed through the question-creation
pipeline (including P2-T4 dedup enforcement).  Good rows are committed even if
other rows fail (partial success).  A downloadable error report is generated
for any rows that errored, were exact duplicates, or had near-duplicate warnings.

Column mapping
--------------
Submit ``mapping`` as a JSON array::

    [{"source_column": "Question", "target_field": "stem"}, ...]

If ``mapping`` is ``[]`` (the default), column names in the file must exactly
match the canonical target field names (as in the downloadable template).

Global scope
------------
Rows with ``scope=global`` require ``super_admin`` role.  Non-admins get a
per-row error for those rows; the rest of the batch is unaffected.

get.description: Return durable progress and the final row-level import result.

Download the full row-level report for a completed durable import.

Legacy one-hour in-process report tokens remain readable for imports completed
before the background-job migration.

post.description:
Bulk approve, reject, or archive a list of questions.

Each question is processed independently (partial success).  Provide the
current ``row_version`` for each question to satisfy optimistic locking.

Mixed scope batches
-------------------
Org-scoped and global questions may appear in the same batch.

* Org-scoped questions: any ``coaching_admin`` or ``super_admin`` may act.
* Global questions (``scope='global'``, ``org_id IS NULL``): only
  ``super_admin`` may act.  A ``coaching_admin`` receives a clear per-row
  error (``GLOBAL_QUESTION_BULK_ACTION_FORBIDDEN``) for each global
  question in the batch; org-scoped questions in the same call are
  unaffected.
Run the real-bank CP-SAT gate synchronously before any future enqueue.
Create a validated paper and schedule prepare_paper atomically.
Freeze the request's complement and enqueue only the requested slots.

get.description: Return committed generation state for reconnect and polling convergence.
Return the exact final solver facts persisted with this version.

A success envelope with no guards involved.

Contrast with ``/health``, which is deliberately **not** enveloped: doc 07 §24.1
describes health checks as an operator/load-balancer surface rather than part of
the API contract, and ``tests/test_health.py`` asserts its bare body.

Raise an exception whose message must never reach the client.

The message is written to look like a leak (a connection string with a password)
so that proof 5 is checking something real: the verification script asserts this
exact substring is present in the server log and absent from the response body.

Proves ``get_current_user`` -> ``get_org_context`` -> ``get_scope`` all ran.

Also the negative half of proof 3: when the guard chain rejects the request, the
:data:`HANDLER_MARKER` line below is absent from the log.

get.summary: Real tenant-scoped read through P1-T5's session + repository
get.description:
Proof 1: a success envelope over data that came out of PostgreSQL.

The path exercised is the whole stack: the guard chain resolved the org, ``get_db``
opened a transaction and issued ``set_config('app.org_id', ..., true)``,
``BaseRepository`` applied the ``org_id`` predicate and the ``deleted_at IS NULL``
filter, and ``EnvelopeRoute`` wrapped the result. Nothing here is mocked.

``Enveloped`` is used so ``meta.pagination`` is populated — the only place in P1-T6
where a handler has an opinion about an envelope field. It still never names
``success``, ``data`` or ``meta.requestId``.

get.summary: Raises EntityNotFoundError for real when the id does not exist
get.description:
Proof 2a: ``EntityNotFoundError`` -> 404.

Raised by ``BaseRepository.get_by_id_or_raise`` against a real query — not
constructed by hand here — so the proof covers P1-T5's code path, not a re-creation
of it.

patch.summary: Raises OptimisticLockError for real on a row_version mismatch
patch.description:
Proof 2b (409) and proof 4 (422), from one endpoint.

Sending a stale ``expectedVersion`` against an existing row makes
``BaseRepository.update`` issue a real ``UPDATE ... WHERE row_version = :n`` that
matches nothing, and P1-T5's own code then distinguishes "absent" from "stale" and
raises ``OptimisticLockError``.

Sending an unknown field, or a wrong-typed one, trips ``BranchUpdateIn``'s
``extra="forbid"`` and produces a ``RequestValidationError`` — the 422 half.

get.summary: Raises TenantContextMissing for real, bypassing the guard chain
get.description:
Proof 2c: ``TenantContextMissing`` -> 500.

This route simulates the only situation in which that exception can occur: code
that opens a session **without** going through ``get_db``, and therefore without a
resolved org. It calls P1-T5's ``get_tenant_session(None)`` directly, which is
exactly what P1-T5's docstring warns about — "the guard chain should have resolved
the org context before the code reached a repository. If this fires in production,
the dependency chain has a hole."

Note what this route does *not* do: it is on the guarded router, so the guard chain
ran and succeeded. The hole is below the guard, which is why the mapping is 500 and
not the 403 that a guard-level failure produces. Proof 3 shows the 403 side.
Proves ``require_roles`` narrows the router default (doc 07 §7.5).

BulkActionIn.title: BulkActionIn
BulkActionIn.description:
Payload for POST /questions/bulk.

Each question_id must be paired with its current row_version for optimistic
locking.  A mismatch on any individual question produces a per-row error
(non-fatal — processing continues for the remaining questions).

Deliberate scope limit
----------------------
This endpoint uses ``get_db`` (tenant-only session).  Global questions
(``org_id IS NULL``) cannot be modified through it — the RLS UPDATE
WITH CHECK clause will deny the write at the database level.  This is
intentional: bulk operations act on the org's own draft queue.  A
super_admin who needs to change the status of a global question must use
the individual ``POST /questions/{id}/approve`` endpoint.

InvitationAcceptIn.title: InvitationAcceptIn
InvitationAcceptIn.description:
``POST /api/v1/invitations/accept`` body — a **public** endpoint.

``full_name`` and ``password`` are ignored when the invited address already has
a user row; see
:func:`app.modules.tenancy.service.accept_invitation` for why the endpoint does
not branch on their presence (it would tell an anonymous caller whether an email
is registered).

``password`` carries the same ``max_length`` as ``LoginIn.password`` and for the
same reason — Argon2id's cost scales with input length, so an unbounded field is
a memory-and-CPU amplification vector on an unauthenticated route.

InvitationAcceptedOut.title: InvitationAcceptedOut
InvitationAcceptedOut.description:
What acceptance returns.

Deliberately **not** a token pair. Acceptance proves control of an invitation
link, not of a password, and issuing a session here would make the emailed link
a bearer credential for the account it just created. The client is expected to
send the user to the login screen, which is also what doc 08's flow does after
registration. Reported as a judgment call.

InvitationCreateIn.title: InvitationCreateIn
InvitationCreateIn.description:
``POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/invitations`` body.

No ``expiresAt`` field — see the module docstring. No ``status`` field either:
an invitation is created ``pending`` and every other value is reached through
an action (accept, revoke), not by assignment.

InvitationCreatedOut.title: InvitationCreatedOut
InvitationCreatedOut.description:
The response to creating an invitation — the only place the token appears.

P1 has no outbound email (doc 07 §4.x lists no mail provider and no queue for
it), so the token is returned to the caller to deliver out of band. Stated as a
gap rather than presented as a design: once a mail sender exists, ``token``
should be removed from this response and the link emailed to the invitee
instead, because returning it to the *inviter* means the inviter can accept
their own invitation and create an account for someone else's address.

InvitationOut.title: InvitationOut
InvitationOut.description:
An invitation, as an allowlist.

``token_hash`` is **absent**, permanently. It is a credential digest, and a
listing endpoint that returned it would let any ``coaching_admin`` who can read
the list also verify guesses at the token offline. The plaintext token appears
exactly once, in :class:`InvitationCreatedOut`, and is never stored.

LoginIn.title: LoginIn
LoginIn.description:
``POST /api/v1/auth/login`` body.

``password`` has a ``max_length`` and it is a denial-of-service control, not
tidiness. Argon2id at m=64MiB is deliberately expensive, and the cost scales with
input length, so an unbounded password field is a request that can be made to consume
an arbitrary amount of server memory and CPU. 1024 is far above any real passphrase.
``min_length=1`` rather than a policy minimum: enforcing password *strength* at login
would reject users whose existing password predates the policy, so strength belongs on
the set-password path (P1-T7's deferred password-reset work), not here.

``org_id`` is optional. See :mod:`app.modules.auth.service` for the full reasoning;
in short, a user with one org can log straight in with a usable token, and a
multi-org user gets an org-less token then calls P1-T8's org-switch endpoint.

REPORTED JUDGMENT — ``email`` is a pattern-checked ``str``, not pydantic's
``EmailStr``. ``EmailStr`` requires the ``email-validator`` package, which is neither
installed in ``backend/.venv`` nor declared in ``pyproject.toml``; using it would
raise at import time and turn a login schema into a boot failure. Adding a runtime
dependency was rejected as out of scope for a task whose brief is authentication
logic. The looser check costs nothing here: an address that is well-formed but
non-existent and one that is malformed both fail to match a row, and doc 07 §20.4
requires them to produce the same generic response regardless. ``users.email`` is
``CITEXT`` with no format constraint in the database either, so this does not weaken
an invariant that existed elsewhere. If RFC-grade validation is wanted later, the
right place is the registration/invitation path P1-T8 owns, with the dependency
declared properly.

LoginOut.title: LoginOut
LoginOut.description:
``POST /api/v1/auth/login`` response body (inside P1-T6's ``data`` envelope).

``expires_in`` is seconds, mirroring OAuth 2.0's ``expires_in``, so the client can
schedule a refresh without decoding the token. It is derived from settings rather
than hardcoded, so retuning ``JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRY_MINUTES`` cannot desynchronise the
advertised lifetime from the real one.

The refresh token is **not** in this body. It leaves only as an ``HttpOnly`` cookie,
per doc 08 line 913, which is what stops a successful XSS from reading it out of a
JavaScript variable.

LogoutOut.title: LogoutOut
LogoutOut.description:
``POST /api/v1/auth/logout`` response.

``revoked`` reports whether a live session was actually found and revoked. It is
informational only: the endpoint returns 200 either way, because a logout that errors
on an already-dead session both fails the caller's intent and tells an attacker which
tokens were real.

MembershipUpdateIn.title: MembershipUpdateIn
MembershipUpdateIn.description:
``PATCH /api/v1/memberships/{membership_id}`` body.

``role`` and ``status`` are both here because doc 07 §4.2's emitted events
include ``membership.role_changed`` and doc 03 §5 gives ``memberships.status``
the ``active``/``invited``/``suspended`` vocabulary — suspending a member is
the only way to revoke access without deleting the row, and ``app_user`` has no
DELETE grant.

Meta.title: Meta
Meta.description:
``meta`` — carries the correlation id and, on list responses, pagination.

Doc 07 §19.3: the ``X-Request-Id`` correlation id is "Included in error
responses (``meta.requestId``)". Doc 08 §10.6 extracts exactly three things from
every response — ``data``, ``meta.pagination``, and ``meta.requestId`` — so both
keys must be present under ``meta`` and nowhere else.

``pagination`` is ``null`` on a single-resource response rather than absent. See
the module note "Every envelope key is always present" for why absence was
rejected.

OrgCreateIn.title: OrgCreateIn
OrgCreateIn.description:
``POST /api/v1/orgs`` body.

``status`` is deliberately absent: a newly created organization is ``active``,
and letting the creator pick ``archived`` at creation time is a state with no
meaning. ``region`` is optional and defaults to the column's
``'ap-south-1'`` (doc 03 §5).

``settings`` is accepted as free-form JSONB because doc 03 §5 defines it as
``jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`` with no schema. A size cap is applied — an
unbounded JSONB body on a create endpoint is a storage-amplification vector,
and P1-T6's ``BodySizeLimitMiddleware`` caps the *request* but not this one
field's share of it.

OrgDeleteIn.title: OrgDeleteIn
OrgDeleteIn.description:
``DELETE /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}`` body.

A body on a DELETE is unusual and is here for one reason: optimistic locking.
ADR-004 makes deletion an UPDATE, and an UPDATE without a ``row_version`` guard
can silently discard a concurrent edit. Sending it as a query parameter was the
alternative and was rejected — a version number in a URL ends up in access
logs, and DELETE with a body is permitted by RFC 9110 §9.3.5.

OrgMembershipOut.title: OrgMembershipOut
OrgMembershipOut.description:
One entry of ``GET /api/v1/orgs`` — an org plus the caller's place in it.

This is the shape doc 08 line 913's login ``orgs`` array wants and the
org-picker screen (doc 08 §6.5) renders: the org's identity, plus *the caller's*
role and branch within it, so the client can label the picker without a second
round trip per org.

``membership_status`` is always ``"active"`` — revision 0027's
``memberships_self_select`` policy makes any other value invisible. It is
carried anyway so that a future relaxation of the policy cannot silently change
what this endpoint means.

OrgOut.title: OrgOut
OrgOut.description:
An organization, as an allowlist.

``subscription_id`` is included because the billing module (P2) needs it and it
is not sensitive; ``deleted_at`` is not, because every read path filters it and
a non-null value would mean the row should not have been returned at all.

OrgUpdateIn.title: OrgUpdateIn
OrgUpdateIn.description:
``PATCH /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}`` body.

Every mutable field is optional so that a caller can change one thing, but
``row_version`` is not — see the module docstring. A body that sets nothing but
``rowVersion`` is rejected by the service with a 422 rather than silently
bumping the version for no change.

OutcomeUpdateIn.title: OutcomeUpdateIn
OutcomeUpdateIn.description: An outcome's chapter placement is immutable.

Pagination.title: Pagination
Pagination.description:
``meta.pagination`` — doc 07 §22.3.

Field names are taken from the doc's JSON exactly: ``page``, ``pageSize``,
``total``, ``hasNext``. Doc 07 §22.4 adds the server-side caps (``pageSize``
default 20, max 100) and cursor pagination (``?cursor=...``). The *dependency* that
parses and clamps those query parameters is deliberately not built in P1-T6: it has
no caller until P1-T8's list routes exist, and the cap belongs next to the query it
constrains. This model only carries the numbers a handler has already decided.

PaperCoverageReport.title: PaperCoverageReport
PaperCoverageReport.description: Final solver facts read verbatim from an immutable paper version.

PaperRealtimeSlotState.title: PaperRealtimeSlotState
PaperRealtimeSlotState.description: One durable assembly checkpoint projected for reconnect reconciliation.

PaperRealtimeState.title: PaperRealtimeState
PaperRealtimeState.description: Durable paper state used after an SSE gap and by polling fallback.

PrincipalOut.title: PrincipalOut
PrincipalOut.description:
``GET /api/v1/auth/me`` — doc 07 §4.2 lists the route and no body for it.

Composed of a profile and the caller's memberships, which is the union of what
doc 08 line 913's login response carries (``user`` + ``orgs``) minus the token.
That symmetry is deliberate: a client that has just refreshed and lost its
in-memory user object can call this and repopulate exactly the same state it had
after login, without a second round trip per org.

``active_org_id`` and ``active_role`` come from the *token's* verified claims,
not from the membership list, so the response also answers "which org am I
currently acting in" — the question doc 08 §9.7's org-switch flow needs answered
after a hard reset.

ProgramAssignmentsOut.title: ProgramAssignmentsOut
ProgramAssignmentsOut.description: Current full-replacement assignment sets for one program.

QuestionApproveIn.title: QuestionApproveIn
QuestionApproveIn.description: Payload to approve a draft question.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Omit or set 'org' for tenant-owned questions. Only super_admin may create 'global' questions.

QuestionCreateIn.title: QuestionCreateIn
QuestionCreateIn.description:
Payload to create any of the 13 question types.

The caller always supplies ``options``, ``answer``, ``rubric`` as plain
dicts — the schema validates the minimum structural requirements per
``qtype`` in the ``@model_validator``. Full per-type field enumeration in
the module docstring.

QuestionCreateOut.title: QuestionCreateOut
QuestionCreateOut.description: Create response: the question plus any advisory dedup warnings.

QuestionCreateWarning.title: QuestionCreateWarning
QuestionCreateWarning.description: Structured, non-blocking warning returned by question creation.

QuestionOut.title: QuestionOut
QuestionOut.description: Full question row as returned by the API.

QuestionUpdateIn.title: QuestionUpdateIn
QuestionUpdateIn.description:
PATCH payload for editing a question.

Editing a *draft* question updates it in place.
Editing an *approved* question forks a new version (BR-8).

``row_version`` is mandatory for optimistic locking on in-place edits;
it is also passed for fork edits so the service can verify the caller
is looking at the correct version before forking.

SavePaperDraftRequest.title: SavePaperDraftRequest
SavePaperDraftRequest.description: Whole-buffer autosave guarded by the last acknowledged draft revision.

SubjectUpdateIn.title: SubjectUpdateIn
SubjectUpdateIn.description: Only the display name is mutable; class and version placement are fixed.

SwitchOrgIn.title: SwitchOrgIn
SwitchOrgIn.description:
``POST /api/v1/auth/switch-org`` body — doc 08 lines 934-938.

Doc 08 gives this endpoint exactly one field, ``orgId``, and that is all it takes.
In particular it takes **no ``role``**: the role for the new token is re-derived
server-side from the caller's membership in the target org. Accepting a role here
would be a self-declared privilege, which is the whole class of bug this endpoint
is most exposed to.

SwitchOrgOut.title: SwitchOrgOut
SwitchOrgOut.description:
``POST /api/v1/auth/switch-org`` response.

Doc 08 line 938 shows only the re-minted access token. ``activeOrg`` is included
as well, for a reason that is a correctness matter rather than convenience: the
role in the new token is re-derived from the target org's membership and may
differ from the role the caller had a moment ago. A client that assumed its old
role survived the switch would render an admin UI for a ``teacher``. Returning
the authoritative pair means doc 08 §9.7's "hard reset" has something to reset
*to* without decoding the JWT client-side.

Same shape as :class:`RefreshOut` minus the cookie, deliberately, so doc 08 §10's
response handling can treat all three token-issuing endpoints alike.

UserOut.title: UserOut
UserOut.description:
The authenticated user, as an allowlist.

``password_hash`` is absent, and its absence is asserted by the verification harness
rather than trusted — an allowlist is only a control if something checks it.

app__common__diagnostics__BranchOut.title: BranchOut
app__common__diagnostics__BranchOut.description:
A branch, as an explicit field allowlist.

Doc 07 §3 requires mappers with an "explicit field ALLOWLIST" and §11.4 the same
for responses. Listing fields rather than using ``from_attributes`` on the ORM
model is what stops a column added later (an internal note, a billing flag) from
silently appearing in an API response.

app__common__diagnostics__BranchUpdateIn.title: BranchUpdateIn
app__common__diagnostics__BranchUpdateIn.description:
A request model in ``extra="forbid"`` mode — doc 07 §6 and §9 Layer 2.

``extra="forbid"`` is the point of this model. Doc 07 §2.10: "An unknown field is
a 400, not a silently ignored key"; §9: "unknown fields are rejected, not
stripped ... Reject: 422 with per-field error details". The status contradiction
between those two sentences is one of this task's reported ambiguities; the
handler for ``RequestValidationError`` resolves it to 422.

Doc 07 §20.1 gives the security reason the mode is not merely tidy: it is the
mass-assignment defence. Without it, ``{"name": "x", "org_id": "<other tenant>"}``
is a request the server would have to remember to ignore.

app__modules__curriculum__schemas__Delet.title: DeletedOut
app__modules__curriculum__schemas__Delet.description: Envelope payload returned after an optimistic, soft delete.

app__modules__programs__schemas__Deleted.title: DeletedOut
app__modules__programs__schemas__Deleted.description: Envelope payload returned after an optimistic, soft delete.

app__modules__tenancy__schemas__DeletedO.title: DeletedOut
app__modules__tenancy__schemas__DeletedO.description:
What a soft-delete route returns.

The delete routes answer **200 with this body**, not 204. Two reasons, both
consequences of decisions made earlier rather than preferences:

* A 204 must have no body, and every response in this application is wrapped in
  doc 07 §22.3's ``{ success, data, meta }`` envelope by ``EnvelopeRoute``. A 204
  would be the one response in the API with no ``meta.requestId``, which is the
  field doc 08 §10.6 extracts from *every* response for correlation.
* ADR-004 deletion is an UPDATE, so there is something true to report: the row
  still exists and is now marked deleted. ``deleted: true`` says that; 204 "no
  content" would imply the resource is gone.
